companion.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2627 - Appendix B (Equality Impact Assessment)
companion.note: Single page EIA. No treasury content. Names Dan Barlow (Head of Finance) as Contact Officer and Cathy Cairns (Finance Manager) as the completing officer, dated 27 January 2026.

paper.note: Self-contained TMS: covering report (pp1-9) plus Appendix A (Strategy, Annexes 1-4, pp10-32). Reviewed by Governance and Audit Committee on 26 January 2026 and referred to full Council 4 March 2026. Rollover strategy — 'no significant changes required' from the 5 March 2025 approved version. Contact block on p9 names Executive Director (Resources) Stephan Van Arendsen (s151) and Contact Officers Cathy Cairns and Shelly Edwards with phone numbers but no email addresses. Neither paper publishes an officer email.

facts.value: 18 PWLB loans totalling £123,931,350 at a weighted 4.4952% (16 MATURITY + 2 EIP)
facts.note: Ties EXACTLY to paper's PWLB £123.931m at 4.495% in Annex 2 (p26) — to the £ on principal and to 3 decimal places on rate. price_book.py --as-at 2025-12-31 returns 16 loans and £117,731,350 due to the known Start-field artefact per EMAIL_TEMPLATE §7; the current-day file is what ties. Reconciliation succeeds and is safe to lead with.

facts.value: PWLB £123.931m at 4.495%; Other loans £6.300m at 4.080%; Short-term nil; Total external £130.231m at 4.475%
facts.note: The £6.300m of 'Other loans' at 4.080% is not PWLB and not itemised beyond the label. The Liability Benchmark chart legend (p13) shows a small 'LOBO loans' strip in the near years above the fixed-rate blocks, suggesting the Other loans are LOBOs. Paper does not publish counterparty, next-option date or strike. £130.231m weighted rate = (123.931 × 4.495 + 6.300 × 4.080) / 130.231 = 4.475 — foots.

facts.value: £285.176m Total CFR at 31/03/2025 Actual; £281.490m Estimate at 31/03/2026; falling to £268.305m by 31/03/2029
facts.note: Includes PFI and finance lease OLTL. Loans CFR strips these out: £180.434m (31/03/25) declining to £167.357m (31/03/29). The Council is deleveraging over the medium-term forecast.

facts.value: £37.359m at 31/03/2026 Estimate; £53.050m at 31/03/2027 Forecast; peaking at £57.056m at 31/03/2025 Actual
facts.note: Paper's sign convention: positive = Loans CFR exceeds external borrowing (i.e. genuine internal borrowing). Stays positive throughout, so the Council is not over-borrowed against Loans CFR itself — the over-borrowing shows against the LIABILITY BENCHMARK, which strips balance-sheet resources back to a £10m liquidity floor.

facts.value: £82.496m at 31/03/2026 Estimate against external borrowing of £140.231m — over-borrowed by £57.735m at that date; forecast £30-33m over benchmark across 2027-2029
facts.note: §1.12 (p12) attributes this to 'cash flows to date have been below the assumptions made when the loans were taken out. Excess borrowing will lead to cash that needs to be invested which thereby increases the risk of the Council losing money.' §1.14 says 'the Capital Financing Requirement will remain above borrowing until 2052'. Distinctive, honestly-disclosed position. Most councils show borrowing UNDER the benchmark (internal borrowing story); Knowsley's is over — a legacy of historic drawings meeting a smaller CFR than expected, not a live policy of over-borrowing.

facts.value: Total authorised limit £360m for 2026/27 (borrowing £240m + PFI/Leases £120m); operational boundary £320m (£210m + £110m)
facts.note: Authorised limit for borrowing steps down 250 → 240 → 220 → 220 across 2025/26 to 2028/29 — consistent with the deleveraging in Loans CFR. §2.2 states currently holds £130.231m of treasury management loans against the £250m 2025/26 limit — comfortable headroom (~£120m under the limit).

facts.value: Refinancing rate risk indicator limits (Upper/Lower): Under 12m 50%/0%; 12-24m 50%/0%; 24m-5y 50%/0%; 5-10y 80%/0%; 10y+ 100%/50%. Paper does NOT publish current actual profile against these limits
facts.note: Our file's derived profile (16 maturity loans priced): under 12m £1.912m (6.75%); 1-2y £15.574m (4.544%); 5-10y £5.736m (4.900%); 10-25y £5.736m (4.600%); 25y+ £84.974m (4.362%). 2 EIP loans totalling £6.8m sit outside the maturity bucketing. Concentration is at 25y+ — 72% of principal on the priced portion. Refinancing exposure inside 5 years is small (£17.5m, ~15%). Do not present as an actual profile the paper endorses — it isn't published.

facts.value: £50.125m at 31/12/2025: Money Market Funds £24.125m at 3.910%, Fund Managers £26.000m at 5.099%. Total weighted 4.527%. Investment balance ranged £71.930m to £35.425m in 2025/26 to date. Forecast closing at 31/03/2026 £67.735m
facts.note: Weighted rate ties: (24.125 × 3.910 + 26.000 × 5.099) / 50.125 = 4.527 ✓. Investment side outyielding external borrowing side at snapshot (4.527 in vs 4.475 out) — a positive net interest position on the visible flows.

facts.value: £26m invested long-term (§5.5). External Fund Managers named on Annex 3 (Jan 2026): M&G Global Dividend, UBS Multi Asset, Schroders Income Maximiser, City Financial Multi-Asset Diversified, CCLA Property, Network Housing, Kames Diversified Monthly Income, UBS Global Income Equity, Fundamentum, M&G Strategic Corporate Bond, Columbia Threadneedle Strategic Bond
facts.note: Paper does not disclose the allocation split across these managers or fair value vs cost. §6.1(e) sets a £40m limit on principal invested beyond year end for 2026/27, 2027/28 and 2028/29 — headroom of £14m against the £26m stated position. §5.5 identifies '£40m of uncommitted working capital that is available for longer-term investment' — so scope to move toward the indicator limit.

facts.value: Pre-2008/09 borrowing: 2% of 31/03/2014 outstanding balance = £1.860m per year fixed (50-year straight-line). Post-2008/09 prudential borrowing: annuity over useful asset life at appropriate PWLB rate. Capitalisation direction expenditure: 20-year asset life
facts.note: MRP policy carried forward unchanged. The annuity method (Annex 4 §3.2) uses 'the 50-year annuity Loan Board rate' as illustrative — a rate we publish daily. IFRS 16 adjustment (Annex 4 §3.4) results in a LOWER MRP charge for PFI arrangements. Nothing controversial or novel in the policy.

facts.value: Upper limit on one-year revenue impact of 1% RISE: £0. Upper limit of 1% FALL: £500,000
facts.note: Asymmetric on the disclosure that the Council has no variable rate borrowing. The £500k downside on a 1% fall is calculated on the highest short-term MMF balances 1 April to 31 December 2025. Unusually clean and precise — most councils publish a symmetric range.

facts.value: Portfolio value-weighted average credit rating: Target A; Actual at 31/12/2025 AAA
facts.note: Comfortably above target. Consistent with £24m of the £50m sitting in MMFs (typically AAAmmf-rated) and Fund Managers holding £26m across advised funds.

facts.value: Paper set 22 December 2025 (Arlingclose forecast, Jan 2026). Bank Rate 3.75% then; central case to fall to 3.25% by Sep-26. Actual: Bank Rate 3.75% at 14 Aug 2026 — unchanged. 20yr gilt central-case Sep-26 4.90%; PWLB 20y certainty at notice 314/26 PM was 6.38%, implying gilt ~5.58% — 60-70bp higher than central case, 150bp above downside. §2.4 short/internal reasoning reinforced by the long-end move; the further-cut short-end call did not play through

source.table: cross-check paper §2.4 + Annex 1 vs current PWLB curve

facts.note: Present as 'your reasoning has been reinforced by what the long end has done since', not as an evaluation of the Arlingclose forecast. The Bank Rate flat-lining at 3.75% is a real point but does not weaken the case for preferring short/internal to long fixed — the long-end elevation is the whole point of the internal-borrowing route.

facts.value: Net DISCOUNT £14,629,705 (13.2% of principal on the £110.931m of maturity loans priced); 11 of 16 maturity loans below par, 5 above; indicative settlement £96,301,645
facts.note: Largest discounts on the recently drawn 4.25%-4.55% coupon 2052-2056 loans (~£1.4m-£3.2m each). Largest premiums on legacy 6.75% coupons maturing 2027-2028. INDICATIVE ONLY. Knowsley has stated NO intention to repay — §5.4.3 keeps invest-to-save under review. Context, not a suggestion. Two EIP loans (£6.8m combined) are not priced by the maturity break-cost engine.

facts.value: £40m limit on principal invested beyond year end for each of 2026/27, 2027/28, 2028/29 (§6.1(e)); £26m long-term invested at time of writing (§5.5); £14m headroom
facts.note: Paper identifies £40m of uncommitted working capital available for longer-term investment (§5.5). Approved counterparties for long-term (Annex 3): LCR Finance PLC 10y, Network Rail 10y, EIB 25y, Wellcome Trust 15y, UK Government 50y. Interesting posture — deploying the over-borrowed cash into longer, higher-yielding positions.

summary.text:
Knowsley's 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy is a self-contained, rollover paper — 'no significant changes required' from the March 2025 version. It carries everything a reader needs: the balance-sheet forecast (Table 1), the liability benchmark table and chart (Table 2, pp10-13), the authorised limits and operational boundary (Table 3), the interest rate indicator, the maturity structure limits, the MRP policy and Annex 4 background, and Annex 2's existing debt and investment snapshot at 31 December 2025. The separate Appendix B on the agenda is only the Equality Impact Assessment — no treasury figures — so the main paper is the whole read.

The loan-book reconciliation ties to the £ and to 3 decimal places on rate. Our own PWLB file for Knowsley holds 18 loans totalling £123,931,350 at a weighted 4.4952% against Annex 2's PWLB total of £123.931m at 4.495%. The Council's paper at §5.4.1 quotes 4.475% weighted across the whole long-term portfolio — blending our PWLB rate with the £6.300m of Other loans at 4.080% reproduces that 4.475% exactly. Balance-sheet identity ties on the paper's own tables at each year-end (285.176 − 123.379 − 104.742 = 57.055 rounded to 57.056 at 31/03/25; 281.490 − 140.231 − 103.900 = 37.359 exactly at 31/03/26).

Two distinctive things make this paper worth writing about. First, the liability benchmark position is unusually candid. Table 2 shows external borrowing running about £57m over the liability benchmark at 31/03/26 and £30m over across the following three years. §1.12 explains it plainly: cash flows since drawdown have been below the assumptions made at the time, and the fixed-maturity loans cannot be repaid without incurring premiums. §1.14 forecasts the CFR remaining above borrowing until 2052. Most councils' papers we have read show borrowing sitting below the benchmark; Knowsley is the other way and has surfaced it themselves. The disclosure is what deserves the compliment, not the position.

Second, §2.4's stated view — 'Short-term interest rates have fallen over the past year, and are expected to fall a little further, and it is therefore likely to be more cost effective over the medium-term to use internal resources or short-term loans instead' — has been partly tested by the eight months since. Bank Rate has held at 3.75% rather than falling to Arlingclose's central-case 3.25%, but the long end has moved further above the central-case gilt yields, so the case for preferring internal or short-term over long-fixed has been reinforced, not undermined. That is worth quoting back with the dates on both sides.

Some smaller points worth flagging in the note but not necessarily the email: the interest rate indicator at §6.1(c) is asymmetric (£0 upper limit on a 1% rise; £500,000 on a 1% fall) — an unusually precise disclosure that all borrowing is fixed and only MMF income is exposed to falls. The £6.3m of 'Other loans' at 4.080% is not itemised but the Liability Benchmark chart legend shows a LOBO strip in the near years, so LOBO-adjacent cross-council context is fair game in general terms. There is £14m of headroom under the price risk indicator's £40m limit against £26m long-term invested, with the paper explicitly flagging £40m of uncommitted working capital available for longer-term investment (§5.5).

Neither the main paper nor Appendix B publishes an officer email address. Stephan Van Arendsen (Executive Director (Resources), s151) approves the report; Cathy Cairns (Finance Manager, 0151-443-3361) and Shelly Edwards (0151-443-3901) are named as Contact Officers; Dan Barlow (Head of Finance) is named on the EIA. All three have phone numbers, none an email. The draft is written to Stephan Van Arendsen with a placeholder for an address — state: 'drafted — needs an address'.

officer.body:
Dear Stephan,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy that went to Council on 4 March, offered ahead of the next treasury report to Governance and Audit. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The paper is unusually clear about a position most reports either bury or don't surface at all, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A cross-check first, because it earns the rest. Our own PWLB file for Knowsley holds 18 loans totalling £123,931,350 at a weighted 4.4952%. Ties to your Annex 2 PWLB total of £123.931m at 4.495% to the pound and to 3 decimal places on rate, and blending our PWLB rate with the £6.300m of Other loans at 4.080% reproduces the 4.475% you cite at §5.4.1 on the total portfolio. So we are looking at the same book. The balance-sheet identity ties too — CFR less external borrowing less other long-term liabilities gives your printed internal borrowing figure at every year-end in Table 1, to 0.001.

The part of the paper worth writing about is §1.12 through §1.14 and how the liability benchmark is presented. Table 2 shows external borrowing running about £57m over the benchmark at 31 March 2026 and £30m over across the three years after. Your paper explains it in one paragraph: cash flows to date have been below the assumptions made when the loans were taken out, the fixed-maturity loans can't be repaid without incurring premiums, and the CFR is anticipated to remain above borrowing until 2052. Most councils we have read either don't publish the benchmark comparison or, where they do, sit under it and tell the internal-borrowing story. Knowsley sits over it and says why. The candour is worth naming, not the position — it makes the rest of the report easier to read. We publish the live PWLB curves that sit behind that benchmark so the crossing point moves with the market rather than being redrawn annually — a natural companion to how the chart on your page 13 is put together.

The strategic call at §2.4 — 'more cost effective over the medium-term to use internal resources or short-term loans instead' — has been part-tested by the eight months since your Annex 1 was written. Bank Rate has held at 3.75% rather than falling to Arlingclose's central-case 3.25% by Sep-26, so the further-cut short-end call hasn't played through. But the long end has moved the other way. At PWLB notice 314/26 yesterday afternoon, the 20-year certainty rate closed at 6.38%, which implies a 20-year gilt around 5.58% against Arlingclose's Sep-26 central case of 4.90%. That's roughly 70bp higher than the central case and about 140bp above the downside case. Whichever way it moves from here, the case for preferring internal or short-term over long-fixed has been reinforced, not undermined. That is not an evaluation of Arlingclose, and we mean it that way — it is the shape of an outcome we can date on both sides.

On the debt-side detail, a couple of smaller points that stood out. The interest rate indicator at §6.1(c) is asymmetric — £0 upper limit on a 1% rise, £500,000 on a 1% fall — with a plain sentence explaining that all borrowing is fixed and only MMF income is exposed. Precise disclosure of that kind is rare across the councils we have read, and it makes the risk shape immediately legible. The £6.3m of 'Other loans' at 4.080% is not itemised in Annex 2, but the LOBO strip in the liability benchmark chart legend on page 13 places them in the near years. We hold no view on the counterparty, the next option date or the strike, and your paper doesn't publish them. What we can add is the cross-council pattern: every LOBO call we have logged across councils in recent months has been refused. Oldham published being offered 6.70% and 7.67%; Wolverhampton 6.19%, 6.21% and 6.26%; several more councils' calls declined. Lenders are testing options now that PWLB rates have risen to meet them, so wherever the option date on the £6.3m sits, the call is more likely than not to be made.

And one for the record on the loan book. On the DMO's premature repayment curve yesterday afternoon, Knowsley's maturity book prices about £14.6m below par on the £110.9m priced, with 11 of the 16 loans in discount and the largest single discounts on the 3.95%-4.55% coupons maturing 2052-2056. Nothing follows from that — §5.4.3 already keeps invest-to-save under review, you've stated no intention to repay, we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, only the DMO can quote, and whether anything is worth doing turns on replacement cost we do not model. It sits alongside the paper's own reasoning rather than pointing anywhere. Your book is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis if it is useful to have alongside, and July sector lending was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin market worth having sight of before you need to be on either side of it, at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

On training, four fit Knowsley particularly. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice for the way the chart on page 13 is constructed and updated. Cost of carry & internal borrowing decisions for the §2.4 reasoning tested above. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator for the invest-to-save reviews at §5.4.3. And Pooled funds (CCLA, multi-asset) for the £26m long-term across the fund managers listed in Annex 3. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts are open for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27, Council, 4 March 2026 (mg72 doc 99365).
